messages:
jordan: Noticed a weird class of failures on new-mini quant canary: structured tool response has trailing array cut off. downstream JSONDecodeError spike ~0.6% across traffic.

aya: Seen it too. Failing bit looks like `confidence_scores` array getting truncated mid-number, e.g. ends with `0.82, 0.9` and then socket closes.

priya: Can you paste a raw example?

jordan: Example from a failing trace:
```
{"tool":"ranker","items":[{"id":"p1","score":0.94},{"id":"p2","score":0.88}],"confidence_scores":[0.99,0.87,0.82,0.9
```

aya: yep that's an open array + missing closing bracket/brace. client sees EOF and throws.

runtime-bot: Canary sampling (5k requests) against new-mini-quant: truncated-array-rate=0.62% (streaming=true, batch=continuous, kvcache=on). With streaming=false: 0.04%.

priya: So streaming strongly correlated. Any recent runtime kernel changes?

jordan: We switched to the small int4 kernels for this build and also increased max-stream-chunk-ms to reduce small-chunk overhead. No other model prompt/schema changes.

aya: Hypothesis: tokenization emits a multibyte sequence at array boundary, which combined with the int4 emission pacing leads to an early stream flush. Could be runtime flush vs finalizer race.

priya: Short-term mitigations: (1) client-side tolerant parser: if JSONDecodeError and trailing characters look like open array/string, try appending closing tokens and attempt parse. (2) increase server-side final flush timeout for streaming responses. (3) mirror canary traffic to non-quant fallback for comparison.

jordan: I'm for (1) and (3) asap. (2) might mask a real bug but worth a canary tweak. I'll open a small SDK patch implementing tolerant-append heuristics for structured outputs only.

ci-bot: quick experiment run: 10k requests, mirrored traffic to fallback fp16 model: new-mini-quant truncated-array-rate=0.58%, fp16=0.01%. Batching off reduced quant-rate to 0.03%.

aya: That strongly points to batch+stream interaction on quant kernel. Priya, can runtime team add token-level emission logs for the int4/int8 kernels so we can see where chunk boundaries align? Need per-token emit timestamp and byte-length.

priya: Will add a kernel-trace flag and run overnight with production-like qps. Also creating a ticket for the runtime engineers to look for premature stream close calls when finalizing token queues.

jordan: For the SDK hotpatch I'm planning: attempt up to 2 soft-repairs before retrying: heuristics include: if ends with `,` append `null]}`, if ends with a numeric fragment append closing digits? (ok joking about last one) realistically: close open arrays/objects and close open strings. We'll log when healer intervenes and surface in console telemetry.

aya: Please ensure healer does not hide real regressions silently. Telemetry needs a flag 'healer_applied' and we should not auto-accept healed outputs for downstream billing-sensitive flows.

priya: Agreed. We'll add a canary rule: healer=false for reserved/dedicated customers by default. SDK default enabled only for hosted dev routes.

jordan: Action list: 
1) SDK soft-healer PR (jordan)
2) Mirror canary to fp16 fallback (jordan/ci)
3) Kernel token-emission trace + ticket (priya)
4) Console metric `truncated_structured_field_rate` (aya)

ci-bot: created job `quant-array-ablation` with 3 arms: int4/int8/fp16 x batching on/off x streaming on/off. Results ETA ~45m.

priya: If ablation reproduces only when batching+streaming are both on, we should triage batching scheduling logic in the continuous batcher.

aya: Also add a small fuzz test that stops the socket after N bytes to see typical suffix patterns — might help to quickly craft the healer rules.

jordan: Will post the ablation summary + healer PR link here. tagging @runtime-team for visibility.

priya: Thanks everyone. If the kernel trace points to a flush call happening before final token enqueued, that's a clear runtime fix path.

jordan: Update: first 5k ablation arm finished — int4+batch+stream = 0.61%, int4+no-batch+stream=0.05%, fp16+batch+stream=0.02%. Pasting the job link in a sec.

aya: Good data. Prioritize rollback of int4 kernels on public canary if we cross 0.5% during peak.

jordan: Noted. Will open rollback if 5m sliding window >0.5%. Will keep thread updated.
